Upcoming Changes

WebSocket port 8443 discontinuation

Last update: October 22, 2026

To support a network infrastructure upgrade, OKX will stop accepting WebSocket connections on port 8443, including Colo connections:

  • Public internet: October 31, 2026
  • Colo: November 16, 2026

Port 443 already works on all affected domains, including Colo, and both ports remain available until these dates.

Breaking change

After these dates, connections to port 8443 will fail. Remove :8443 from your WebSocket URLs. Only the port changes; the host and path stay the same. wss:// uses port 443 by default, and :443 also works. This applies to every path, including /ws/v5/public, /ws/v5/private, /ws/v5/business and, on the Global site, /ws/v5/public-sbe.

  • Public internet, from October 31, 2026
    • Production
      • Before: wss://ws.okx.com:8443/ws/v5/public
      • After: wss://ws.okx.com/ws/v5/public
    • Demo trading
      • Before: wss://wspap.okx.com:8443/ws/v5/public
      • After: wss://wspap.okx.com/ws/v5/public
  • Colo, from November 16, 2026
    • All Colo WebSocket connections on port 8443.

REST API is not affected.

Add error codes

Until these dates, connections on port 8443 receive a notification (event = notice) with the following code once the handshake succeeds. The connection stays open.

Error code Error message
64010 WebSocket port 8443 will be retired soon. Please migrate to port 443.

SBE order entry and private data

Last update: October 28, 2026

OKX plans to introduce Simple Binary Encoding (SBE) services for order entry and private order and fill updates. The services are expected to launch in the demo trading environment on November 11, 2026 and in the production environment in early December 2026.

Existing REST and JSON WebSocket APIs will remain unaffected.

New SBE services

Service Production URL Demo trading URL XML schema
Order entry wss://ws.okx.com/ws/v5/trade-sbe wss://wspap.okx.com/ws/v5/trade-sbe okx_sbe_trade_2_0.xml
Private data wss://ws.okx.com/ws/v5/private-sbe wss://wspap.okx.com/ws/v5/private-sbe okx_sbe_private_1_1.xml

The login method is the same as that of the existing SBE Market Data service. Authentication is completed during the WebSocket HTTP Upgrade request by providing the API key and signature in the request headers.

JSON control messages use text frames with opcode 1, while SBE messages use binary frames with opcode 2.

Compared with the JSON services, the fields in SBE messages are streamlined. Refer to the XML schemas for the complete message layouts and field definitions.

XML schema updates

The XML schemas have been updated ahead of launch. Please use the latest versions above to generate your encoders and decoders.

Order entry: okx_sbe_trade_2_0.xml

  • Schema id changes from 1 to 2; version remains 0, and semanticVersion changes to 2.0.0. The message layouts change; regenerate your encoders and decoders using this schema.
  • Single and batch place-order requests add optional rpiPxRound (RPI price rounding) and reduceOnly fields. Single and batch amend-order requests add optional rpiPxRound.
  • In single and batch place/amend requests, expTime is renamed to expTimeUs. In all place/amend/cancel responses, ts is renamed to tsUs. These fields continue to use microseconds.
  • Single and batch place-order responses remove instIdCode; subsequent fixed fields shift forward and their field IDs change.
  • Single place/amend/cancel responses add the variable-length UTF-8 error message msg.
  • Batch place/amend/cancel responses rename the data group to results, with entries in request order (up to 20). They add the sMsgDetails group containing per-order error messages (sMsg), linked to results by the zero-based resultIndex, and a batch-level msg. Both msg and sMsg use varString16, a variable-length UTF-8 string with a uint16 length prefix.

Private data: okx_sbe_private_1_1.xml

  • Schema id remains 1; version changes from 0 to 1, and semanticVersion changes to 1.1.0.
  • The orders message adds optional reduceOnly (booleanEnum: FALSE=0, TRUE=1) and avgPxMantissa (average executed price mantissa, using pxExponent). Both fields have sinceVersion="1".
  • In orders, fillTime, uTime, and cTime are renamed to fillTimeUs, uTimeUs, and cTimeUs. In fills, ts is renamed to tsUs. Their units remain microseconds, and the renamed fields retain their field IDs and types.

SBE order entry

The order entry service will support the following operations:

  • Place order and place multiple orders
  • Amend order and amend multiple orders
  • Cancel order and cancel multiple orders

Batch operations will support up to 20 orders. SBE order entry will support CASH and CROSS trading modes. Clients that require another trading mode should continue to use the JSON WebSocket trading API.

SBE private data

The private data service will support the following channels:

  • orders: Publishes an update when an order is created or its state changes.
  • fills: Publishes order-book fill events and is available to VIP4 and above users.

Neither channel will publish an initial snapshot. Subscription requests and responses will remain in JSON format, while channel data will be encoded in SBE. The orders channel will support filtering by instType; instIdCode is not required. For the fills channel, instIdCode is also not required.

Signal Clone — New API endpoint

Last update: May 14, 2026

OKX is adding API support for the Signal Clone (Order Sharing) feature. API traders can now generate a universal sharing link programmatically by passing an order ID. The link encodes the order parameters (instrument, side, leverage, price, TP/SL, etc.) server-side. Recipients who open the link will have those parameters prefilled in the OKX App trading panel.

This feature is scoped to USDT-margined perpetual contracts. Signal Clone must be enabled for the account.

Create signal link

  • Create signal link
  1. A new endpoint POST /api/v5/copytrade/create-sgl-link is added.
  2. Pass orderId and instId in the request body. The order must belong to the requesting account.
  3. Only USDT-margined perpetual contracts (instId ending in -USDT-SWAP) are supported. Other instrument types will return an error.
  4. Returns a shortLink — a universal OKX App link that can be shared with others to prefill the trading panel with the order parameters.
  5. Rate limit: 10 requests per second per user.

Request example

POST /api/v5/copytrade/create-sgl-link
body
{
    "orderId": "3556007031710728192",
    "instId": "ADA-USDT-SWAP"
}

Request parameters

Parameter Type Required Description
orderId String Yes Order ID. Must belong to the requesting account.
instId String Yes Instrument ID, e.g. BTC-USDT-SWAP. Only USDT-margined perpetuals are supported.

Response example

{
    "code": "0",
    "data": [
        {
            "shortLink": "https://www.okx.com/ul/1xJ7nV"
        }
    ],
    "msg": ""
}

Response parameters

Parameter Type Description
shortLink String Universal sharing link. Recipients can open this link in the OKX App to have the order parameters prefilled in the trading panel.

2026-10-27

New bbo-rpi-tbt order book channel for RPI best bid and ask

Added the public WebSocket channel bbo-rpi-tbt. It pushes the best RPI bid and ask (1 depth level) built from all resting RPI orders, including hidden RPI orders that cross the organic best bid/ask or each other and are therefore excluded from books-rpi. Push cadence and data format follow bbo-tbt: a 1 depth level snapshot on the initial push, then a snapshot every 10 ms when it changes. No login or trading fee tier is required.

  • WS / Order book channel

Request parameters

Parameter Type Required Description
> channel String Yes Channel name
bbo-rpi-tbt

Push data parameters

Parameter Type Description
> asks Array of Arrays Order book on sell side
For bbo-rpi-tbt, only RPI orders are returned, including hidden RPI orders. Returns [] when there is no RPI order on the sell side.
> bids Array of Arrays Order book on buy side
For bbo-rpi-tbt, only RPI orders are returned, including hidden RPI orders. Returns [] when there is no RPI order on the buy side.

2026-09-30

Instruments channel push optimization

OKX has optimized the push behavior of the Instruments channel.

In some scenarios, the channel now uses incremental pushes instead of full pushes and delivers only instruments whose data has changed.

In the future, OKX may switch additional scenarios from full pushes to incremental pushes without further notice. Clients should update their local instrument cache by instId when receiving a push and should not assume that every push contains the full set of instruments.

USD spot trading pair migration

OKX has consolidated the USD and USDC spot order books. Affected Crypto-USD spot instruments have been delisted, and API clients must use the corresponding Crypto-USDC instruments.

Migration requirements

  • Requests that previously used a Crypto-USD instrument ID must now use the corresponding Crypto-USDC instrument ID.
  • This applies to REST APIs and WebSocket channels whose request parameters include instId or instIdCode.
  • Crypto-USD instrument IDs are not mapped to Crypto-USDC instrument IDs. Requests and subscriptions that continue to use a delisted Crypto-USD instId or instIdCode may fail or return no data.
  • Responses use the actual Crypto-USDC instrument ID or instrument ID code. Clients should update request construction, response parsing, subscription management, instrument caches, and any logic keyed by instId or instIdCode.

Trading quote currency

The default value of tradeQuoteCcy is the quote currency in instId. Therefore, changing only instId from Crypto-USD to Crypto-USDC changes the default trading quote currency from USD to USDC.

To continue trading with USD after migrating to the corresponding Crypto-USDC instrument, explicitly set tradeQuoteCcy to USD.

Scenario Before the migration After the migration
Continue trading with USD "instId": "Crypto-USD"
tradeQuoteCcy omitted		 "instId": "Crypto-USDC"
"tradeQuoteCcy": "USD"
Trade with USDC "instId": "Crypto-USD"
"tradeQuoteCcy": "USDC"		 "instId": "Crypto-USDC"
"tradeQuoteCcy": "USDC" or omit tradeQuoteCcy

Before submitting an order, obtain the supported quote currencies from tradeQuoteCcyList through GET / Get instruments.

Activate USDC trading

  • Added POST / Activate feature. Call this endpoint only if order placement returns error code 54109; otherwise, you do not need to call it.
  • Added error code 54109. Refer to REST API error codes for details.

2026-09-29

Global Liquidity Program API v2

Three new REST endpoints are added under /api/v5/users/glp/v2/ to support the Global Liquidity Program (GLP). Authenticated users can query GLP enrollment status, real-time performance metrics, and weekly assessment history. A sub-account API key retrieves the master account's GLP data.

New endpoints

  • GET / Get GLP v2 overview
  • GET / Get GLP v2 assessment details
  • GET / Get GLP v2 performance history

2026-09-15

RPI maker minimum notional amount thresholds

RPI maker orders (ordType: rpi or elp) now use separate minimum notional amount thresholds by product type. Orders below the applicable threshold are rejected with error code 54051. Effective in production from September 15, 2026.

Minimum thresholds by product type

Product type Minimum notional amount
SPOT 500 USD
FUTURES 2,000 USD
SWAP 5,000 USD

Applies to all REST and WebSocket trade operations:

  • POST / Place order
  • POST / Place multiple orders
  • POST / Amend order
  • POST / Amend multiple orders
  • WS / Place order
  • WS / Place multiple orders
  • WS / Amend order
  • WS / Amend multiple orders

2026-08-26

New endpoint: Get Delta hedge currencies

Some tokenized assets trade under a different currency name than the underlying they track, e.g. XAAPL and AAPL, or BETH and ETH. Because these pairs share one underlying asset, a position in one can hedge a position in the other. This mapping is now available programmatically.

  • New endpoint:
    • Get Delta hedge currencies
